verdict.summary: Posting messages is self-serve in minutes. Reading messages at a useful rate needs a Slack Marketplace listing: new unlisted apps can only read history once a minute, 15 messages at a time.

whoYouNeed.role: A member of a Slack workspace you control
whoYouNeed.why: Every Slack app is created inside one workspace, and you test it there first.

whoYouNeed.role: 10 or more real customer workspaces (for reading messages)
whoYouNeed.why: Slack only reviews Marketplace apps that already have 10 active installs.

steps.title: Sign in to Slack's app dashboard
steps.plain: Log in at api.slack.com/apps with the workspace that will own the app.
steps.whyHuman: Signing in is yours to do.

steps.title: Create the app from a pre-filled link
steps.plain: One link opens Slack's 'Create app' screen with Composio's redirect address and the usual agent permissions already filled in. Change the name, pick your workspace, remove permissions you don't need, and create.
steps.technical: Uses Slack's manifest URL (api.slack.com/apps?new_app=1&manifest_json=...). Bot scopes pre-filled: chat:write, channels:read, channels:history, users:read. Redirect URL: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback (check it matches your Composio auth config).

link.label: Create the app with settings pre-filled

steps.title: Check the redirect address and permissions
steps.plain: Under OAuth & Permissions, confirm the redirect address matches your Composio auth config and the permission list is what your agent needs.
steps.technical: Redirect URLs must use HTTPS and cannot contain '#'. Bot scopes and user scopes are listed separately. Composio's auth config lists the scopes it requests.

link.label: Open your app, then OAuth & Permissions

steps.title: Switch on public distribution
steps.plain: Without this, only your own workspace can install the app. Open Manage Distribution, tick off Slack's checklist, and click Activate Public Distribution.
steps.technical: Checklist requires OAuth handling and HTTPS on every request URL. No review happens at this step.

link.label: Open your app, then Manage Distribution

steps.title: Copy the client ID and secret into Composio
steps.plain: From Basic Information, copy the client ID and client secret into your Composio Slack auth config.
steps.whyHuman: The secret is a password for your app. Pasting it yourself keeps it out of any agent's chat history.

steps.title: Install in a second workspace to test
steps.plain: Connect a different workspace through Composio to confirm other teams can install it.

evidence.note: Slack asks Marketplace applicants to test outside the development workspace. We apply the same advice here.

steps.title: Reach 10 active workspaces (reading only)
steps.plain: Get the app installed and used in at least 10 workspaces in the last 28 days. Until then you can't apply for the Marketplace, and reading stays throttled for new installs.
steps.whyHuman: These have to be real customers or pilots, not your own test workspaces.

steps.title: Submit to the Slack Marketplace (reading only)
steps.plain: Submit from your app's settings with a demo video (install, sign-in, use, uninstall), a test account with dummy data, and a reason for each permission.
steps.whyHuman: The video and test account need a person. An agent can draft the permission justifications.

link.label: Open your app, then Submit to Slack Marketplace

steps.title: Slack reviews your app (reading only)
steps.plain: A preliminary review takes up to 10 business days, then a functional review takes up to 10 weeks for new apps. Resubmitting during the preliminary stage resets your place in the queue.

evidence.note: Slack gives upper bounds only. The 14-day minimum is our estimate.

forks.effect: Stop after step 6. Throttling only affects reading history and threads, so no Marketplace listing is needed.

nuances.title: Unlisted apps read Slack slowly
nuances.detail: Since May 29, 2025, commercially distributed apps outside the Marketplace get 1 request a minute and at most 15 messages per call on conversations.history and conversations.replies. Internal apps keep 50+ requests a minute and 1,000 messages.
nuances.ifStuck: For pilots, read only recent messages or run as an internal app in each customer's workspace. For scale, plan the Marketplace listing early.

sources.title: Slack changelog: rate limits for non-Marketplace apps

evidence.note: Slack's changelog exempts existing installs of older apps. Slack's FAQ reportedly extends the limits to existing installs from March 3, 2026; we have not confirmed that on Slack's own page.

nuances.title: The redirect address must be HTTPS
nuances.detail: Slack rejects plain http:// redirect addresses, including for local testing.
nuances.ifStuck: Use Composio's HTTPS redirect address, or a tunnel such as ngrok for local work.

nuances.title: Ask for fewer permissions
nuances.detail: Workspace admins weigh the permissions you request when deciding whether to approve your app.
nuances.ifStuck: Remove scopes your agent does not use yet. You can add them later.

config.redirectUriNote: Use the HTTPS redirect URI shown in your Composio auth config.

scopes.name: channels:history
scopes.plain: Read messages in public channels the app is in.

useCases.label: Post messages and replies
useCases.summary: Create the app and switch on public distribution. No review. Steps 1 to 6.

useCases.label: Read channel history or threads (summaries, search, triage)
useCases.summary: Unlisted apps created after May 29, 2025 get 1 request a minute and 15 messages per request on conversations.history and conversations.replies. Lifting that needs a Marketplace listing: 10+ active installs, then up to 10 business days plus up to 10 weeks of review.

useCases.label: Only inside your own company's workspace
useCases.summary: Internal apps are not throttled and need no distribution or review.

sources.title: Slack changelog: rate limits for non-Marketplace apps

composio.note: You can connect users today with Composio's own Slack app while yours is set up or in review. Users see 'Composio' on the consent screen, rate limits are shared with other Composio customers, and polling triggers run at most every 15 minutes. Switch to your own app when it is ready.

limits.note: Composio's own Slack app is not Marketplace-listed yet (Composio says its review is in progress), so reading history through it hits the same limits as any unlisted app, including at most 15 messages per request. It does not get you around the wait for reading.

existingApp.summary: Add Composio's redirect address under OAuth & Permissions, then paste the existing client ID and secret into Composio. Existing installs keep working.

reReviewTriggers.effect: New scopes only apply after each workspace reinstalls the app.

reReviewTriggers.trigger: Your app is already in the Slack Marketplace and you change permissions
reReviewTriggers.effect: Resubmit for review: the functional review takes up to 6 weeks for published apps.

reReviewTriggers.trigger: Your app is unlisted and gets new installs
reReviewTriggers.effect: Installs made after May 29, 2025 are throttled when reading history, even if the app itself is older.

blockers.symptom: Slack won't let you submit to the Marketplace
blockers.cause: Apps need at least 10 active workspace installs before they can be submitted.
blockers.fix: Distribute the app directly (shareable install link) to customer workspaces until you reach 10 active installs, then submit.

blockers.symptom: Your Marketplace submission is sent back
blockers.cause: Common reasons: scopes for features you have not built yet, scopes you cannot justify, install problems, or bugs that block testing. Reviewers cannot get into your workspaces.
blockers.fix: Address each point of the feedback in your app settings and resubmit. Request only the scopes you use today, and give reviewers a test account and a way to install the app themselves. Your queue place resets if you resubmit during the preliminary review.

blockers.symptom: A customer can't install your app
blockers.cause: Their workspace requires admin approval for apps, or has restricted yours.
blockers.fix: Ask the customer to request the app and have a workspace owner or app manager approve it. Restricted apps cannot be requested at all.
